description: The repository shall maintain this catalog as the canonical record of Constellation requirements, ownership, implementation evidence, verification, milestones, release scope, sources, and known limitations.
verification: Manual structural review of the catalog header and populated requirement rows
notes: The schema preserves the common Taskyon and Syncpeer columns and adds Taskyon compatibility, milestone, and target-release tracking. This is a catalog policy rather than application behavior, so it is implemented without a regression-test claim.

description: Status shall distinguish unmet requirements (`planned`), implemented requirements without maintained regression tests (`implemented`), and implemented requirements with focused regression tests in the regular test workflow (`tracked`).
verification: Manual review of the status definitions and the 2026-09-29 0.1 status audit
notes: The verification field names the focused regression test and regular runner for tracked rows. One-off manual, Playwright-only, emulator-only, build-only, or live-service checks remain useful evidence but do not by themselves qualify a row as tracked. Implemented rows record code or policy evidence without claiming maintained regression coverage. Transient pass/fail outcomes belong to the test runner rather than this catalog.

description: Every requirement shall classify its relationship to Taskyon as native protocol reuse, layered application behavior, a runtime adapter, or local Constellation behavior.
verification: 2026-09-29 catalog audit of taskyon_compat classifications
notes: Allowed values are native, layered, adapter, and local. This classification policy is implemented but is not itself regression-tested.

description: Requirements shall use foundation, web-preview, 0.1, 0.1.1, 0.2, 0.2.1, 0.3, 0.4, post-1.0, or future milestones to express implementation order independently from release scope.
verification: Manual structural and release-classification review of the catalog (2026-10-06)
notes: Target release defines product inclusion; milestone defines implementation order. Release 0.1.1 covers browser QR hardening, peer consent and presentation, source-approved single-recipient access, peer-bound return approval and map decluttering. Release 0.2 adds local co-movement list grouping and pinned public Taskyon dependencies; spaceship peer identicons target 0.2.1. Existing 0.2 Groups/delegation, 0.3 link-management and 0.4 group-cache requirements retain their targets. This planning convention is implemented without an application regression-test claim.

description: Every requirement shall use target_release 0.1, 0.1.1, 0.2, 0.2.1, 0.3, 0.4, post-1.0, or future so delivered behavior and later product scope can be filtered without duplicating the catalog.
verification: Manual structural and release-classification review of the catalog (2026-10-06)
notes: Release 0.1 remains the first usable product and retains its historical implementation and verification evidence. Planned 0.1.1 acceptance is defined in release-0-1-1-product-acceptance; it tightens single-recipient and return approval and adds explicit name consent, one peer list and map decluttering. Local co-movement list groups and direct pinned public Taskyon dependencies target 0.2; Taskyon spaceship identicons target 0.2.1. Existing Groups/delegation remain 0.2, link-management 0.3 and group-cache work 0.4. New acceptance criteria remain planned until implemented and tested.

description: Release 0.1 shall contain the complete first usable product scope; compatible 0.x releases may harden that scope from field evidence, and the same product shall become 1.0 only after satisfactory real-world browser, Android, relay, privacy, battery, and adverse-network validation.
verification: Manual review of release-scope and maturity policy
notes: Version 1.0 is a maturity promotion rather than a smaller or separate feature set. Release 0.1 includes the reported field fixes; 0.2 adds general Groups and recipient delegation; 0.3 carries link-management and deferred 0.1.1/1.1 items; group last-known caching moves to 0.4. Sensor, location, share, and transport wire versions evolve independently from product release numbers. This is release policy, not an application regression-test target.

description: Release 0.1 shall ship the hosted browser app, an installable Tauri Android app, and installable Linux desktop artifacts consisting of an AppImage and a Flathub-ready Flatpak, and shall let two real people use independently generated links to share live locations across supported clients, scan received links from QR codes, privately offer a timed share-back link to the original source, observe freshness and connected viewers, and stop or revoke access without developer tooling. Own and followed map areas shall use the same zoom-based dot fallback and color; an in-app diagnostic suite shall exercise sharing through real transports with synthetic paired sessions and explicit guided native checks.
verification: tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop local relay;owned-adapter API 29/36 Android/browser return flows and strict two-Android-plus-desktop-browser three-way replay;Android debug APK build;2026-09-29 fresh sandbox AppImage and Flatpak builds;AppImage Xvfb launch smoke;2026-09-29 hosted-relay API 36 Android/browser full flow and Tauri desktop dev preview;2026-10-01 synthetic signed arm64 release build;yarn test:pages local Pages preflight;AppImage payload Xvfb window smoke;yarn licenses:inventory;tests/sharing-diagnostics.spec.ts local-relay browser lifecycle/expiry;docs/RELEASE_0_1_ACCEPTANCE.md external acceptance checklist
notes: Browser local-relay sharing, independent links, reload recovery, and an authenticated private return offer have test evidence. The owned Android location adapter passed API 36 one-shot/watch smoke and API 29/36 background-source to browser-viewer location, locked-screen update, private browser-to-Android return offer, process-restart recovery, presence, revocation, and shared-text intake. A strict local-relay replay with two API 36 Android devices and a desktop browser passed all three Star links: each Android peer received both other locations and each source showed two viewers. Force-stopping and relaunching one Android app on an API 36 emulator restored both saved follows and both received locations. This resolves the earlier mixed-viewer acceptance blocker in the tested environment; the strict three-way desktop peer was a browser preview, not packaged Tauri desktop. Separately, a Tauri desktop development viewer received a browser location via the hosted relay and appeared in source presence on 2026-09-29. Simultaneous multi-link continuity under adverse networks and physical-device recovery remain unverified. The owned adapter passed the full managed Android/browser flow on API 29 and API 36; direct native one-shot/watch smoke remains API 36-only. The current AppImage was rebuilt from the locked Nix flake in the sandbox and stayed alive through a 10-second Xvfb launch smoke; the same sandbox produced the current Flatpak bundle. Packaged Flatpak live-sharing and ordinary host-launch integration remain unverified. A managed API 36 Android/browser hosted-relay two-way flow passed on 2026-09-29, though one prior run had a WebView debugger stall after wake. Representative real-network checks belong to the 0.1 release-candidate acceptance; signed release, packaged desktop sharing, physical-device acceptance, final license review and publication remain project work. A TLS mismatch was observed on 2026-09-29; the hosted GitHub Pages app was confirmed working on 2026-10-03. Group invitations/member sharing and recipient re-sharing are deferred to 0.2. Repository-side 0.1 work completed on 2026-10-01: per-link battery/metered network policy with mixed-link emulator acceptance, a local GitHub Pages preflight wired into CI, a full synthetic signed arm64 release build with verified signature and checksum, a dependency license inventory, and a packaged AppImage payload startup smoke. The remaining acceptance is manual/external only: the real production signing identity and physical-device install/upgrade, human-authored final Flathub manifest plus packaged desktop launch with the normal desktop keyring and visual checks, representative real-network/NAT checks, and the two-person cross-client acceptance. The repository owner confirmed the hosted GitHub Pages app is working on 2026-10-03. In-app received-link QR scanning is included in 0.1; a synthetic-camera browser regression exercises decoding and the ordinary preview flow. Android camera permission and physical-device capture still need release acceptance. The return-group approval, one-time share-back, status/history notices and Android creation/status fixes are required for 0.1. The in-app diagnostic suite automates synthetic two-device sharing over real networks; guided native cases do not replace physical-device acceptance. Basic signed install/upgrade, QR capture, packaged desktop and representative-network checks remain 0.1 release acceptance; the full long-running vendor Android matrix is the separate 1.0 maturity gate.

description: Constellation shall be distributed under the MIT License with copyright held by Xyntopia.
verification: LICENSE text;package metadata;scripts/license-inventory.test.mjs;scripts/artifact-license-inventory.test.mjs;yarn licenses:inventory (2026-10-01: 245 JavaScript production packages on x86_64, two MPL-2.0 including the installed optional node-datachannel binary; 504 Cargo packages with five MPL-2.0 and no unknown licenses);yarn licenses:inventory (2026-10-04: 244 JavaScript production packages, 242 permissive and two MPL-2.0; 504 Cargo packages, 499 permissive and five MPL-2.0);scripts/artifact-license-inventory.test.mjs strict fail-closed coverage;prior artifact triage: APK entries and 191 AppImage libraries classified with no unclassified bundled library
notes: The MIT license applies to Constellation source and metadata. Taskyon snapshots and map/software dependencies retain separate notices; the Linux secret-service crate is MIT OR Apache-2.0. scripts/license-inventory.mjs resolves installed package roots directly, so exports that hide package.json no longer drop dependencies: on 2026-10-01 it found 245 JavaScript production packages on x86_64 (243 permissive; node-datachannel and its installed @node-datachannel/linux-x64-gnu optional binary are MPL-2.0 but Node-only and not bundled in the app artifacts) and 504 Cargo packages (499 permissive, five MPL-2.0: cssparser, cssparser-macros, dtoa-short, option-ext, selectors). The 2026-10-04 inventory found 244 JavaScript production packages (242 permissive, the same two MPL-2.0 Node-only packages) and 504 Cargo packages (499 permissive, the same five MPL-2.0 packages). r-efi lists MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later and can be used under the permissive alternatives. scripts/artifact-license-inventory.mjs inspects the Android APK entries and the extracted AppImage payload; the AppImage bundles the GTK/WebKitGTK stack (191 libraries, mostly LGPL-2.1-or-later) and the APK ships AndroidX/Kotlin with META-INF notices. This remains a triage, not a legal opinion: full license texts, LGPL source-offer/relinking conditions, Android/Gradle and Flatpak runtime notices, and final publication review remain human gates.

description: Constellation shall consume Taskyon-owned package boundaries for shared protocol and P2P capabilities through released versions, complete provenance-recorded vendored snapshots, or reproducible commit-pinned public upstream subpackages; Constellation-owned location behavior shall remain local and the repository shall never import sibling source paths or build artifacts.
verification: yarn test:vendor;yarn build;scripts/package-boundary.test.mjs (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: Release 0.1 uses complete provenance-recorded snapshots of @taskyon/protocol, @taskyon/p2p-core and @taskyon/diagnostics as workspace packages. Generic changes are made in Taskyon first and synchronized; released package dependencies replace these snapshots later. The p2p-core snapshot includes a real local-relay reservation expiry regression and typed reservation lifetime configuration; stopping the relay clears AutoNAT polling. scripts/package-boundary.test.mjs scans application, script, and test imports to keep Taskyon imports on the published package names, reject sibling, absolute, vendored-source, and repository build-artifact paths, and require matching upstream provenance and package manifests. Planned 0.2 upstream-public-taskyon-dependencies replaces copied snapshots with independently consumable subpackages from the public Taskyon GitHub repository; upstream fixes and exact source revisions must be pushed there before Constellation pins them. Existing snapshot evidence does not verify that future dependency strategy.

description: Constellation shall use pinned Taskyon-owned TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and Vite configuration through a supported shared package.
verification: corepack yarn format:check;yarn lint;yarn test;yarn test:android:config;yarn build;scripts/browser-environment.test.mjs
notes: Deferred beyond 0.1. The standalone 0.1 repository intentionally owns pinned local TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and Vite configuration and validates it in CI. A published Taskyon-owned configuration package remains later integration work to eliminate copied configuration drift.

description: Taskyon shall expose generic MapLibre and PMTiles behavior through a reusable package that does not require the complete Taskyon UI graph or contain location-domain semantics; Taskyon-specific range caching shall remain available through an injected source adapter.
verification: Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre test;Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre typecheck;Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre build
notes: Deferred beyond 0.1. Constellation 0.1 owns its thin MapLibre/PMTiles integration and location overlays. The generic Taskyon map package exists upstream but is not published or installed by Constellation; adopting the supported package remains later integration work.

description: A fresh Constellation checkout shall install, test, and build without a Taskyon sibling checkout; future Taskyon integration shall use independently consumable released packages or commit-pinned public upstream subpackages rather than relative sibling imports or dependencies on another local checkout.
verification: .github/workflows/ci.yml quality job: corepack yarn install --immutable;corepack yarn lint;corepack yarn test;corepack yarn build
notes: Constellation is self-contained through complete vendored Taskyon package snapshots with recorded provenance and documents its standalone web, desktop, and Android workflows. Application code imports package names only; published versions will replace the workspace snapshots without changing imports. The planned 0.2 public upstream dependency transition must preserve standalone installation, package-name imports, lockfile reproducibility and CI builds without private remotes or sibling worktrees.

description: Constellation shall supersede the unauthenticated in-memory Deno and SSE location prototype after equivalent basic live sharing is verified.
verification: Basic browser and Android live-sharing evidence is recorded by the 0.1 acceptance and interoperability rows
notes: The Constellation implementation has equivalent basic live sharing and supersedes the unauthenticated in-memory Deno/SSE prototype. The prototype remains only a UX reference; this supersession decision has no dedicated maintained regression test.

description: Taskyon shall define a transport-independent read-only sensor service for dynamically described sensors and authenticated observations.
verification: Taskyon:@taskyon/protocol sensor client/server unit test;Taskyon:@taskyon/protocol type-check and build
notes: The versioned descriptor, observation, subscribe, unsubscribe, and event contract exists in Taskyon. Generic authentication, grants, advertisements, signatures, and peer transport integration are deferred; Constellation 0.1 uses its narrow authenticated location-sharing stream, not a general sensor service.

description: A peer shall declare zero or more stable sensor endpoints without requiring a centrally fixed list of sensor kinds.
notes: Deferred beyond 0.1. Declarations are descriptive and grant no authority by themselves.

description: Each sensor endpoint shall identify a versioned profile or canonical schema revision, value shape, units, quality metadata, stream behavior, and owning service principal.
notes: Generic descriptors are deferred beyond 0.1; release 0.1 validates only Constellation's location observations and does not execute custom sensor semantics.

description: The sensor model shall support interoperable Taskyon standard profiles and dynamically declared custom schemas through the same descriptor mechanism.
notes: Profile interpretation remains separate from transport and discovery.

description: Every observation shall bind its sensor identifier, descriptor revision, source principal, monotonic sequence, capture time, value payload, and quality metadata to an authenticated source envelope.
notes: Generic signed sensor envelopes are deferred beyond 0.1. The 0.1 location-sharing stream retains its existing authentication and sequence checks; this row does not describe those as generic sensor signatures.

description: Authorized consumers shall receive current and subsequent observations through one bounded Taskyon protocol stream with explicit cancellation and backpressure.
verification: yarn test:unit;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop two independent sources;vendor/taskyon/p2p-core/src/stream.test.ts accepted-byte backpressure regression
notes: An authenticated stream per viewer has bounded framing and queues, subscribe/unsubscribe, heartbeat cleanup and transport close. A newly created share seeds its first observation from a still-fresh current fix, so a stationary source need not wait for another GPS event. Observations are not persisted. Taskyon backpressure waits for drain without repeating accepted frames; a focused synthetic test reproduces the old duplication and passes after the upstream fix.

description: A separately authorized sensor-history capability shall stream a bounded time range without exposing provider paths or an unbounded query surface.
notes: Constellation initially permits at most the latest 30 minutes for remote location views.

description: A signed expiring service advertisement shall identify protocol and descriptor revisions, routing information, limits, and expiry without revealing private Space membership.
notes: Deferred beyond 0.1. Advertisement proves neither authorization nor correct behavior.

description: Space or transient-share grants shall independently authorize publish-own and read-current operations for explicit sensors and bounded scopes.
notes: Generic grants are deferred beyond 0.1. The 0.1 bearer link remains a narrow location-view capability; read access never implies publication, history access, delegation, device control, or Space administration.

description: Writable attributes and device commands shall remain outside the first sensor protocol and require a separate future command capability and authorization review.
notes: A generic sensor declaration must not become an unrestricted remote-control surface.

description: Sensor endpoint, profile, attribute, and event concepts shall preserve a clean future mapping to Matter while making no initial Matter wire-compatibility claim.
source: Connectivity Standards Alliance Matter specification;Thread Group resources
notes: A Matter bridge will be a separately authorized and tested adapter.

description: Constellation shall treat libp2p as connectivity fabric and the Taskyon sensor protocol as the application layer rather than coupling sensor semantics to one network transport.
notes: Generic Taskyon sensor-service layering is deferred beyond 0.1. The 0.1 application retains its narrow location-sharing protocol over libp2p; this is not Thread protocol implementation.

description: Constellation shall define a versioned location profile for its authenticated sharing stream, including source-owned disclosure precision, bounded coordinates, uncertainty, capture and expiry times, and optional altitude, heading, and speed; a later generic Taskyon sensor envelope may carry the same profile.
verification: src/location/locationObservation.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: The validated application profile is local to Constellation so Taskyon does not acquire a product-specific location package. Mapping it into the generic Taskyon sensor envelope and peer authorization are deferred beyond 0.1.

description: Location observations shall use source-owned monotonic sequences and explicit capture and expiry times so receivers can reject replay and display stale state honestly.
verification: src/location/locationObservation.test.ts;src/location/browser.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: The browser source emits monotonic sequence and explicit capture/expiry times; the viewer rejects non-increasing sequences and recomputes live, delayed, and stale map state. Wall-clock timestamps alone never establish authority.

description: A publishing device shall adapt sampling to movement, elapsed time, requested detail, power state, and a maximum interval through simple battery-versus-detail presets.
notes: The 0.1 Android service uses a five-second/five-metre movement baseline with a rate-limited fresh fix on viewer arrival. Measure battery use before choosing adaptive presets; this is a 0.1.1 improvement.

description: When an authorized viewer subscribes and the source's last fix is older than thirty seconds or absent, the source shall request one fresh location fix, rate-limited to one request per minute per device. The last known observation remains viewable as stale while the request is pending; movement-only background sampling remains the baseline.
verification: src/location/browser.test.ts;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop reconnect;nix develop --command yarn build:android:debug:x86_64-emulator;Android one-shot device acceptance pending
notes: A successful authenticated sensor subscription triggers a single current-position request only when the last fix is old. Android's foreground service selects the network provider when enabled, otherwise GPS; API 29 uses requestSingleUpdate. It times out after twenty seconds. Doze and provider availability can still delay or prevent an update; no guaranteed delivery time is claimed. The source restoration path also adopts an already acquired fresh GPS fix so a viewer need not wait for further movement.

description: The source shall choose device accuracy, one-kilometre approximate, or city-sized very coarse disclosure independently for each active share and shall always see the active choice.
verification: src/shareDraft.test.ts;tests/share-flow.spec.ts desktop and mobile;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop
notes: New shares default to approximate and projection happens independently per share. Device accuracy is an explicit no-added-blurring choice, not a promise of precise GPS; the wire value remains exact for compatibility, and a coarse-only Android grant retains its actual reported uncertainty. The active list names very coarse separately. The third-choice mobile button and final action fit the Pixel 5 emulated viewport; native visual acceptance remains pending.

description: Release 0.1 shall offer a third source-selected sharing preset that publishes a stable city-sized uncertainty area of at least 20 km radius, without naming a city or changing the source's own map position. Its randomized center must scale with the selected radius rather than remaining within the one-kilometre mode's small offset; the transmitted location and redeem response remain approximate for older viewers.
verification: src/shareDraft.test.ts;src/location/approximation.test.ts;src/android/backgroundSharing.test.ts;yarn test;yarn test:android:config (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: The 20 km minimum uses radius-scaled random center placement and the existing per-share hysteresis and overlap; after a temporary poor-accuracy enlargement a new region can shrink toward the preset. Protected source settings survived browser reload in the focused relay test. P2P delivery through the unchanged approximate wire contract passed; the Android x86_64 debug APK compiled. Android on-device and physical-device sharing remain unverified. Adjustable radius is future UX work. City-sized areas reduce precision, not anonymity.

description: For each share using approximate precision, the source shall publish a soft circular uncertainty region with a default one-kilometre radius and keep that region stable while the reported position and its reported GPS uncertainty remain safely contained.
verification: src/location/approximation.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: Each in-memory share independently draws cryptographically secure random center and threshold values; there is no grid, reusable seed, share-secret derivation, or per-sample randomization.

description: The source shall create a new randomized uncertainty region only after crossing its private hysteresis threshold consistently, or earlier when needed to preserve containment; consecutive regions shall overlap by at least 75 percent of their area, and poor GPS accuracy shall enlarge the advertised radius rather than exclude the reported uncertainty.
verification: src/location/approximation.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: Two consecutive threshold crossings, immediate containment repair, overlap enlargement, and poor-accuracy enlargement are implemented. Browser region control state is encrypted and restored per link; restart behavior is covered by the browser relay test, but native region restoration and an explicit continuity test remain pending.

description: Approximate observations shall expose only the advertised region and freshness needed to render it; they shall not expose exact coordinates, grid identifiers, random inputs, private thresholds, speed, or heading.
verification: src/location/approximation.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: The published approximate payload contains only the randomized area center, containing radius, source sequence, and freshness timestamps; altitude, heading, speed, threshold, random inputs, and exact coordinates are omitted.

description: The UI and documentation shall state that approximate sharing reduces precision but does not provide anonymity or a formal privacy guarantee, and that long trajectories, known places, screenshots, copied observations, or colluding recipients can still reveal sensitive patterns.
verification: scripts/product-policy.test.mjs;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality);tests/share-flow.spec.ts desktop (.github/workflows/ci.yml browser-regression)
notes: About explicitly states that approximate and very-coarse sharing reduce precision without making the source anonymous, and names long trajectories, known places, screenshots, copied observations, and colluding recipients as residual risks. Received approximate locations render one area without a center point while larger than the marker; below that screen size they collapse to one dot at the advertised region center, using the same rule as own locations.

description: A viewer shall distinguish live, delayed, stale, expired, revoked, and unavailable location state instead of silently presenting old coordinates as current.
verification: src/sharing/sharingRuntime.test.ts;scripts/product-policy.test.mjs;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality);tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop (.github/workflows/ci.yml browser-regression)
notes: The viewer keeps the most recent observation in memory across a temporary disconnect and marks its age as stale or delayed while the authenticated share remains active; intermittent updates do not mean the share ended. Show on map appears only after an observation exists, and details show its last update time and age. Explicit revoked/expired close reasons and separate former-share history are tracked in share-lifecycle-history. Received coordinates are still not persisted across app restart.

description: Constellation shall present one local person identity with independently named and revocable device identities, each of which may publish its own authorized location.
notes: The Taskyon person/device hierarchy is deferred beyond 0.1; local peer identity and editable device labels remain part of 0.1 sharing. A device identity does not independently grant broad access to user or Space data.

description: A new source or viewer shall receive a local device identity without registration, hosted account authentication, or disclosure of a stable identity to other link recipients.
verification: tests/p2p-share.spec.ts independent-link source-identity and reload regression (.github/workflows/ci.yml browser-regression);src/sharing/privateStore.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: No account or hosted authentication is required. Each newly generated outgoing link owns a fresh Ed25519 libp2p source identity, so its PeerId and dialable addresses are not stable across independently generated links; the per-link private key is restored only from protected encrypted local state so a surviving link keeps working after restart. The viewer/device identity remains local and separate. Pre-migration links that lack a stored per-link source key retain their legacy shared source identity until revoked because changing their PeerId would invalidate the existing bearer link. Deleting local application data may destroy identities and active shares; account recovery is outside 0.1.

description: Background publishers shall receive a narrow device-bound principal and publish-own grant without receiving Space administration or read access to unrelated sensors.
notes: The generic Taskyon principal/grant model is deferred beyond 0.1; Android background location sharing remains an explicit 0.1 requirement and must not gain unrelated Space access.

description: Missing membership, grant, publication, or distribution policy shall deny location access.
notes: Named Space authorization is deferred beyond 0.1. Transient location-share access still requires its existing explicit bearer capability; global discovery must never advertise future Space membership.

description: The initial UI shall expose shares and connections rather than requiring users to understand Space keys, overlays, grants, or service advertisements.
notes: Security mechanics remain inspectable in diagnostics and advanced details.

description: A future named family or friends group shall be an independent collaborative Space rather than an extension of the user's default personal Space.
notes: Location publication remains opt-in per Space.

description: Ordinary group members shall be able to publish their own location and view members who currently choose to share, while administrators alone manage membership.
notes: Joining a group never starts location sharing automatically.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support promotion and revocation of multiple administrators and explicit ownership transfer.
notes: Administration remains separate from ordinary membership and device control.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support an offline recovery secret without putting root keys or reusable administrator credentials in invitations, links, logs, or QR codes.
notes: Recovery requires bootstrap access to an authorized provider or rendezvous network.

description: Equivalent location data shared into different transient share scopes shall be encrypted independently to reduce provider-side correlation.
verification: src/sharing/sharePayloadCrypto.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: Each transient share has an independent 256-bit bearer secret. A domain-separated HKDF key encrypts every location payload with AES-256-GCM and a fresh IV bound to that share ID before it enters the libp2p stream, so equivalent observations in separate shares have independent ciphertext even when they use the same transport connection. Generic named Spaces remain deferred; ciphertext size, timing, and ordinary connection metadata are not claimed to be unlinkable.

description: Persistent Space enrollment shall use short-lived single-use QR or invite links with out-of-band fingerprint confirmation and existing-administrator approval.
notes: This enrollment flow is distinct from pre-authorized transient location links.

description: A location link shall create a narrow encrypted share scope and read grant without enrolling receivers as people, devices, or members of a collaborative Space.
verification: src/sharing/shareProtocol.test.ts;src/sharing/sharePayloadCrypto.test.ts;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop;.github/workflows/ci.yml quality and browser-regression
notes: A link grants only its source location sensor on authenticated per-viewer streams. Location payloads are additionally encrypted with a share-specific application-layer key derived from that link's random secret, independent of the libp2p connection encryption. Browser grants persist encrypted across reload; named Space integration remains future work.

description: The share URL shall place the bearer capability in its fragment and shall not expose it to HTTP requests, referrers, logs, analytics, or messenger link-preview fetches.
verification: src/sharing/shareLink.test.ts;yarn test (.github/workflows/ci.yml quality)
notes: The canonical share URL serializer preserves bearer and owner-proof fields when selecting advertised transport addresses; its focused round-trip and owner-proof test covers this boundary. Fragment-only encoding and browser session-only redemption are implemented; the visible fragment is cleared after connection. Native viewers retain explicit acceptance. Deployed hosting and Android handoff remain unverified.

feature: Immediate browser view and optional keep
description: A browser visitor opening a valid share fragment shall see the sender's live location immediately without an acceptance modal or own-GPS request. The connection shall be session-only until Keep following persists it; the sender may observe viewer presence and connection metadata.
verification: tests/p2p-share.spec.ts browser preview and saved-follow reload;tests/share-flow.spec.ts invalid fragment;src/sharing/sharingRuntime.test.ts;.github/workflows/ci.yml browser-regression
notes: Immediate browser preview and optional encrypted save are implemented. The sender name is learned after redemption and never added to the URL; local nickname is not sent in redemption. Saving can begin own GPS but denial does not block saved following. A preview notice offers Stop preview; malformed links show a redacted error. Expired-link and mobile browser acceptance remain unverified.

description: Android shall accept valid Constellation HTTPS links through ACTION_VIEW and text/plain ACTION_SEND from apps such as Signal, while desktop Tauri shall route a pasted valid link directly to the approval flow. Native links require a View location tap before redemption, followed by editable nickname confirmation.
verification: yarn test:android:config;owned-adapter Android debug APK build;managed API 29/36 warm/cold ACTION_SEND and return offers;strict two-Android-plus-desktop-browser local-relay follow-save replay;src/platform/sharedText.test.ts
notes: Android ACTION_SEND text is consumed once and a valid URL from surrounding text enters native approval; ACTION_VIEW uses the existing deep-link adapter. Desktop paste enters the same approval flow. The owned-adapter API 29 and 36 APKs passed warm/cold ACTION_SEND approval and both Android peers saved links from the desktop and the other Android peer during strict three-way replay, resolving the prior stalled Tauri callback in that test. Native approval opens an editable nickname prompt before persistence; dismissing it leaves a preview. Repeated warm ACTION_SEND for a second link, ACTION_VIEW, hosted App Links (the public hostname served an assets.taskyon.space-only certificate on 2026-09-29), and physical-device acceptance remain unverified; in-app camera scanning of received links is included in 0.1 and tracked separately by qr-link-scanning.

description: A device's durable trail shall contain only samples generated by that device and shall never append locations received from another peer.

description: A device shall append self-generated samples to bounded daily text journals containing a versioned header and one authenticated base64url ciphertext envelope per line.

description: Journal envelopes shall authenticate device identity, format version, sequence, capture time, and previous-envelope commitment so truncation, reordering, replay, and corruption are detected.

description: Completed daily or size-bounded journals shall rotate into signed immutable segments suitable for verification and optional blind replication.

description: Self-history shall default to thirty days and offer shorter periods or keep-until-deleted; cleanup shall remove complete expired segments and their keys or envelopes.

description: Selected storage services may retain opaque source-authored immutable trail segments without receiving plaintext, Space membership, or decryption authority.

description: A source may grant remote viewers access to at most the latest thirty minutes of its trail through a bounded memory-only stream.

description: Official clients shall not write another device's received trail to persistent storage or re-advertise it as a local sensor history.

description: Hosted relays, mesh routers and Space bridges shall forward opaque end-to-end encrypted traffic without receiving location plaintext, reusable share capabilities, or implicit collaborative Space membership.
notes: A router that decrypts or republishes data is a distinct service principal requiring an explicit grant; ordinary routing never grants sensor access.

description: In release 0.2 a publisher may explicitly allow opted-in devices in a quick-share group to cache only its latest application-encrypted observation per rotating opaque mailbox, for at most 24 hours and never beyond the share expiry. A cache grant never grants location-viewing authority.
notes: Release 0.1 remains memory-only and live P2P. Group sharing is a prerequisite; named Taskyon Spaces are not required for this first group cache. The one-minute freshness expiry and longer last-known retention are distinct; receivers label older observations stale. Ordinary peers have a default capacity of 100 different share mailboxes, not 100 samples per source. Cached plaintext and reusable share capabilities are forbidden. Revocation cannot erase plaintext previously viewed and deletion notices may arrive late.

description: The first relevant group-sharing flow shall ask each publisher whether its own share may use encrypted last-known caching; caching is off by default and each potential storage device separately opts in to host cache duty. The prompt shall explain 24-hour maximum retention, source expiry, and connection-metadata visibility without claiming anonymity.
notes: One group member's cache consent never enables caching for another member's publication. A group cache may be a member without being permitted to view a hub-mode location.

description: Opted-in reachable group devices shall rotate the active cache role through bounded leases with an acknowledged overlapping handoff, favoring charging devices while balancing extra duty over time. No cache volunteer or interrupted handoff shall degrade ordinary live sharing or be represented as a guaranteed always-online service.
notes: The role rotates cache availability work, not all battery use from location acquisition or P2P presence. Duplicate ciphertext during handoff is deduplicated by authenticated source ordering; every provider applies bounded quotas and expiry.

description: Viewing, publishing, caching ciphertext, relaying, delegating, and group administration shall be separate grants. Direct peers, quick-share groups, delegated peers, friends of friends, and strangers discovered globally have progressively weaker relationship trust but no implicit authority from their tier alone.
notes: Release 0.2 only enables explicitly opted-in group caches. A later version may let one device cache for several separate friend networks with isolated keys, mailboxes, quotas, and grants; unrelated networks must not learn one another's membership. Stranger caching requires explicit admission and abuse controls, not a reputation score based on self-reported capacity.

description: After less-trusted caching is safe, an optional headless Constellation peer may join the same blind-cache protocol with a configured capacity up to 100000 latest share mailboxes, without becoming a special trusted server or gaining location-viewing authority.
notes: This is not required for 0.2. Packaging, durable storage, quotas, and abuse resistance remain deployment work even though the wire protocol is shared with ordinary cache peers.

notes: Intermediate routing belongs to Taskyon P2P beneath the sensor protocol. This is not part of release 0.1.

description: Future location sessions shall be able to traverse mixed LAN, Bluetooth, WebRTC, native-socket and relay links without introducing transport-specific location messages or weakening authorization.
notes: Bluetooth and LAN are planned link adapters, not currently implemented transports or claims of Thread, Zigbee or Bluetooth Mesh wire compatibility.

description: A future reachable LAN or mesh gateway shall be able to carry multiplexed upstream traffic and route separate encrypted viewer sessions to several authorized downstream peers without becoming a location viewer by default.
notes: The source retains per-viewer capacity, presence and revocation semantics. Plaintext redistribution requires a separate explicit service grant.

description: Future mesh routing may retain only the newest bounded encrypted location frame across intermittent links and shall discard it at the source-controlled expiry without constructing a trail or durable received-location history.
notes: Blind routers receive no location plaintext. Longer queues and history remain separate capabilities.

description: A future opt-in mode shall let an authorized device carry bounded end-to-end-encrypted latest-location records across disconnected Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi groups, synchronize by authenticated inventory and deduplicate by source-scoped opaque record ID and sequence, then forward eligible records on reconnection to another local mesh or the Internet.
notes: A hiking group may exchange encrypted last-known positions across short-range hops; a member who leaves can carry eligible records to another group kilometres away. This is asynchronous ferrying, not a guaranteed 500 m Bluetooth link or real-time mesh. Source-controlled expiry, bounded storage, quotas, revocation checks when reachable, freshness labels, and loop/duplicate suppression still apply. Longer retention or trails require a separate explicit grant; the ordinary 0.2 cache remains latest-only and capped at 24 hours. An offline-only transport choice must not silently upload on Internet reconnection.

description: Cross-group forwarding and viewing shall be independently authorized: a carrier may copy opaque records only under a source or group forwarding grant, and members of a newly encountered group may decrypt them only under pre-authorized read or explicitly delegated emergency-view grants with bounded sources, recipients, precision and expiry.
notes: Merely meeting another group must never make the original group's positions readable. If the injured source cannot grant access while offline, the necessary emergency read/delegation policy must already exist; exact policy and consent UI require a separate threat-model decision. Metadata visible to carriers and recipients must be documented. No life-safety delivery claim without field validation.

description: Future native clients shall offer explicit Bluetooth-only and local Wi-Fi-only sharing modes as well as automatic transport selection, carrying the same authenticated Taskyon logical messages and encrypted cache records without requiring cellular or Internet connectivity.
notes: Local Wi-Fi includes LAN and device-to-device options where supported. Strict offline modes must not fall back to cellular, Internet relays, or later upload without an explicit policy change. Discovery, pairing, MTU, permissions, Android background limits, battery cost, supported hardware, and multi-hop routing require device-level validation. No claim of Bluetooth Mesh interoperability follows from using Bluetooth links.

description: The transport-independent mesh envelope may later support explicit external long-range radio adapters such as LoRa or other locally permitted sub-GHz hardware for low-rate store-and-forward traffic, without changing location, chat, or authorization semantics.
notes: No specific band, range, throughput, or off-the-shelf phone support is promised. Fragmentation, replay protection, power use, device support, and regional spectrum and duty-cycle rules require a separate design and field review before implementation.

description: Future routing and caching shall maintain local, decaying, role-specific reliability scores from directly observed delivery, availability, and protocol behavior; cryptographically demonstrable invalid messages or grant violations may trigger immediate local quarantine, while mere silence or poor radio links affect route preference rather than proving malice.
notes: Do not accept self-reported capacity or unverified accusations as reputation evidence, or publish a global blacklist. Bound scoring by identity/role, resist churn and Sybil abuse with admission and quotas, allow decay and recovery, and keep alternative routes and redundant cache holders so excluding one peer does not partition the group. No scoring system can reliably distinguish intentional packet loss from an intermittent link or guarantee quick global removal of an attacker.

feature: Optional Tor connectivity and anonymity study
description: Evaluate an optional Tor-routed Internet transport for native or headless Taskyon/Constellation peers and onion-hosted bootstrap or relay endpoints, with a strict privacy mode that prevents direct-path and ancillary-network fallbacks before promising anonymity.
notes: Tor requires Internet and cannot replace disconnected Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi links. Browser WebRTC, DNS, bootstrap, map-tile requests and other direct traffic can reveal IP or link activity; simply adding a Tor proxy to the current browser app is not an anonymity guarantee. Evaluate metadata, identity/link correlation, timing, latency, Android integration, and failure behavior before choosing an implementation; end-to-end encryption remains necessary.

description: A future Constellation chat shall use Taskyon's versioned messaging contracts, FRP streams and libp2p logical network to exchange authenticated end-to-end-encrypted one-to-one and group messages over direct, relayed and permitted offline transports, with separately consented bounded store-and-forward delivery.
notes: Taskyon's current diagnostic P2P chat is not a production encrypted offline messenger. Generic message/envelope semantics belong upstream in Taskyon; Constellation keeps its UI and policy local. Chat needs per-conversation bounded message queues, expiry, deduplication, ordering and delivery state, not the latest-location-only cache; separate cache and read grants and metadata limits apply. Offline delivery is best-effort until field validated.

description: Future synthetic tests shall exercise Bluetooth-only and Wi-Fi-only isolation, disconnected cache-carrier handoff, cross-group read and forward grants, expiry and revocation during outages, peer quarantine and recovery, route diversity, and chat delivery without plaintext at blind caches.

description: A reusable Group invitation shall let a person join and see locations that members have chosen to publish to the whole Group, without publishing their own location automatically. Any online member shall be able to authenticate and admit the holder of a valid unexpired invitation even when the creator is offline. Admission shall authorize automatic authenticated P2P connections and reconnections with other admitted members, without additional per-connection permission prompts. A member shall separately choose whether to publish their own location to the whole Group or to selected individual members; only those recipients may see a private publication. Already-admitted members shall exchange live updates over direct member-to-member P2P sessions, with ordinary libp2p transport relays allowed, so the creator need not stay online for those sessions.
notes: Deferred as a complete Group flow to 0.2: invitation, discovery, admission, member connections, selective publication, and revocation must work together before Group appears as a usable mode. Group is the user-selected UI name for this all-member sharing topology. The creator is neither a location-data hub nor a required online admission server. Group connection consent is not location-publication consent; the join screen must explain that fellow members can learn membership and online presence through automatic connections even when location publication is off. Group-scoped rendezvous must locate online members; each admission must verify the invitation, bind the joining peer identity, and disseminate membership to existing members without distributing location-publication authority. The current one-way link is not Group membership. Member-to-member sessions may use a transport relay but do not route plaintext through the creator. Invitations and membership grants require bounded expiry. Revocation is eventually propagated across connected members, cannot erase past observations, and cannot be promised instantaneous across disconnected partitions; peer-specific publication grants must be checked by each publisher. Do not claim a strict global member cap while independent online members can admit concurrently without coordination. Named Taskyon Spaces remain later integration.
